documentation: docs/ci_cd.md -> 'Publish-blocking required checks'. This file is the ONE canonical, machine-consumed inventory of the repository-required product checks that must be successful, for the exact product SHA, under trusted workflow identity, before any mutable `latest` release, Docker image, or immutable version-tag artifact is published. .github/scripts/verify_publication_gate.py is the only consumer; .github/scripts/verify_required_ci.py checks parity between the branch-protection required set, ci.yml's frozen `main-publish-gate` array, the `main-publication-required-checks` gate, and release.yml's `validate-release-sha`. These parity checks are PR-mutable drift detection, not a trusted-policy freeze of the hosted gate; see docs/ci_cd.md.

required_checks.rationale: The publishing jobs live in this same workflow run and each declares `needs: test` plus `needs.test.result == 'success'`, so the main-path aggregate is proven in-run rather than through the Actions API. The version-release verifier has no such in-run relationship and binds the `Tests` check run to every canonical ci.yml push run for the exact tag target, without inheriting failures from unrelated publisher jobs in that workflow.

This protected workflow is a PR-admission gate and cannot be given a push trigger by an ordinary change. The publication gate resolves the unique merged pull request associated with the product commit, requires that pull request to target main, binds its head SHA to the product commit's second parent, and then requires every canonical pull_request_target run of this workflow at that PR head to succeed. A direct push has no associated pull request and therefore does not publish.
Runs unconditionally on every push to main; ci.yml's frozen `main-publish-gate` array cannot be extended by a pull request, so publication evidence is collected by `main-publication-required-checks`.

Issue #4302 added an unconditional `push: main` trigger so the required check yields exact-main-SHA evidence instead of merge-group-only evidence. On a `main` push the frozen trusted-base relevance job takes its `--force-run` branch, so the full suite always executes; `merge_group` is not force-run and still classifies its change set, which is why merge-group evidence alone was not sufficient.
